ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Own a core operational domain at an early-stage financial technology company, such as customer operations, payment operations, or financial crime operations. You will build its processes, metrics, tooling, and automations, partnering directly with the COO and working closely with Product and Engineering.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Handle operational cases directly at first to identify process gaps and establish meaningful performance metrics.

 - Design and launch production automations, then validate them with live workflows and measure their impact.

 - Scale automated agents across your domain while reserving human review for high-risk or complex decisions.

 - Work alongside Product and Engineering to specify agents and build operational tools.

 - Create and maintain escalation paths, standard operating procedures, and performance metrics.

 - Improve throughput while keeping operational processes efficient and headcount stable.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - At least 3 years of experience building products or processes in banking, fintech, payments, or crypto, or consulting experience with regulated financial services.

 - Experience shipping production workflow automations or agents, including AI or LLM-based systems where applicable.

 - Hands-on operational experience, such as queue management, case handling, or transaction processing.

 - Experience owning end-to-end operational domains, including process design, SOPs, KPI definition, and tooling.

 - Ability to define and optimize operational metrics and collaborate with Product and Engineering to build systems.

 - Relevant experience in regulated financial services, with exposure to compliance, risk, financial crime, payments, or settlement operations beneficial.

 - Experience building or scaling operations in an early-stage or high-growth environment is valuable.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary: $180,000 to $220,000 USD annually. Visa sponsorship is available.


LOCATION

On-site in New York, New York, United States. Candidates based elsewhere must be willing to relocate.

About InstaLILY 
 InstaLILY is an AI products and infrastructure company that puts execution at the frontier of enterprise AI. That work begins with Lily™ , the world's first AI Forward Deployed Engineer, which learns how a business works, builds the software it needs, and goes live in days. It does not leave when the work ships; it stays and keeps the software working as the business changes. Lily runs wherever the work happens, in the cloud, on-premise, or at the edge, through InstaLILY's Small Data Center, built with NVIDIA technology. Founded in 2023 by Amit Shah and Sumantro Das, InstaLILY has raised nearly $100 million from Energize Capital, Insight Partners, and Home Depot Ventures. Headquartered in New York, with offices in San Francisco, London, and Toronto, InstaLILY serves leading companies across construction, industrial distribution, logistics, healthcare, and other operationally intensive industries. Learn more at https://instalily.ai/ .
 The Traction 
 Revenue grew 5x over the past year, and Lily has driven over $200M in new annual sales for a single customer. We serve some of the largest operators in our industries, including SRS Distribution (part of The Home Depot family), United Rentals, and Henry Schein, and we work closely with the Google DeepMind and NVIDIA ecosystems.
 How We Work 
 We work in small teams with real ownership: clear problems, direct access to the customers whose work you're changing, and room to ship. Your code runs in live production systems inside billion-dollar operations, so you see your impact directly. People who do well here want that proximity to the work. We're growing fast, and the people who join now shape what this company becomes. Everything runs on three principles: Customers, Culture, and Code.
 The Role 
 You'll be the named InstaLILY point of contact for a portfolio of post-pilot enterprise customers. You'll run their QBRs and executive briefings, lead account plans, surface new use cases to deploy, and be the senior partner they call when complex decisions come up. The role spans current deployments, new use cases, expansion conversations, and everything in between.
 You'll be in weekly contact with your customers, working across their CIO, CTO, and revenue leaders on how AI reshapes their operating model. You don't carry a quota. Success is customer outcomes and expansion driven by deep partnership.
 You'll take handoffs from our Sales team and Growth Analysts and own the customer motion from that moment forward. The handoff experience is one of the most important things this role gets right.
 You'll report to our Chief Growth Officer.
 What You'll Do 
- Account ownership. Manage a portfolio of post-pilot customer accounts day-to-day across QBRs, exec briefings, account plans, and customer success activities.
- Transformation engagement. Help each customer think strategically about how AI changes their operating model, not just adoption of features, but transformation of how their team works.
- Expansion. Identify new use cases for each customer based on their workflows, industry context, and where AI can drive operational impact. Drive expansion ARR through deeper deployment.
- Strategic collaboration with product. Bring customer insight into product decisions. What you hear shapes our roadmap. You'll help guide zero-to-one feature development and ensure the product evolves with what customers actually need.
- Cross-functional coordination. Coordinate with Engineering and Product to make sure your customers get what they need to succeed.
- Playbook contribution. Help build and refine the structured playbook Strategic AI Partners run across customers. What works, what doesn't, what should be standardized.
- Customer presence. Travel to customer sites as needed for in-person work with customer teams and executives.
 What You'll Need 
- 7-10 years of Customer Success, strategic account management, or consulting experience. Ideally at an enterprise SaaS

 At Really Great Reading, we are building a bright, diverse, and passionate team dedicated to leading the industry in improving literacy scores nationwide. With nearly two decades of leadership bringing the Science of Reading to thousands of schools, we design innovative products, training, and materials that transform how educators teach and how students learn. Here, we empower our team with the tools, support, and professional growth opportunities they need to thrive in a collaborative, forward-thinking environment—where your work truly makes a difference.

 At Really Great Reading, we believe every child deserves to learn to read — and that great instruction, thoughtfully supported, makes that possible. The  Senior Literacy Outcomes & Strategic Partner  exists at the intersection of that belief and the real work of transforming literacy outcomes at scale.
 This is a role for someone who has sat in district leadership, knows what it takes to move systems, and is energized by helping educators find solutions that truly work. You will partner closely with our Revenue and Customer Success teams to guide high-value district and state-level partnerships — translating the Science of Reading into practical, lasting impact for students.

 As a  Senior Literacy Outcomes & Strategic Partner , you will serve as our most trusted instructional voice in complex, high-stakes partnership conversations. You will advise senior district and state leaders, support our go-to-market strategy, and help ensure that every district we partner with is set up for real, measurable success.

 Serve as Our Expert Voice in Strategic Partnerships 
- Partner with Account Executives and Customer Success teams on high-value, complex opportunities
- Deliver compelling, outcome-driven presentations to Superintendents, Chiefs of Academics, Literacy Directors, and State DOE leaders
- Ensure a seamless, trust-centered transition from the sales relationship into implementation and long-term partnership
- Serve as a thought leader in the Science of Reading and literacy transformation communities
 Drive Pipeline and Market Presence 
- Represent Really Great Reading at conferences, leadership convenings, and state literacy events
- Collaborate with Sales and Marketing on campaigns, outreach, and high-impact initiatives that generate a qualified pipeline
- Build strong relationships with district leaders and stakeholders throughout the sales cycle and early implementation stages
- Align efforts to support quota attainment for strategic segments/accounts
- Track and contribute to pipeline-influenced and revenue-supported
- Identify and contribute to expansion opportunities within existing accounts
- Partner with leadership and revenue teams to strengthen strategic proposals, renewal strategies, and long-term partnership value
 Translate Expertise into District and State Impact 
- Demonstrate deep expertise in the Science of Reading, structured literacy, and evidence-based foundational literacy instruction

- Help districts define success criteria, implementation benchmarks, and measurable outcomes aligned to their strategic goals and funding priorities
- Connect product capabilities to real student achievement outcomes — and help districts see and communicate that impact
- Contribute to the development of customer success narratives, impact metrics, and evidence of program effectiveness

About InstaLILY 
 InstaLILY is an AI products and infrastructure company that puts execution at the frontier of enterprise AI. That work begins with Lily™ , the world's first AI Forward Deployed Engineer, which learns how a business works, builds the software it needs, and goes live in days. It does not leave when the work ships; it stays and keeps the software working as the business changes. Lily runs wherever the work happens, in the cloud, on-premise, or at the edge, through InstaLILY's Small Data Center, built with NVIDIA technology. Founded in 2023 by Amit Shah and Sumantro Das, InstaLILY has raised nearly $100 million from Energize Capital, Insight Partners, and Home Depot Ventures. Headquartered in New York, with offices in San Francisco, London, and Toronto, InstaLILY serves leading companies across construction, industrial distribution, logistics, healthcare, and other operationally intensive industries. Learn more at https://instalily.ai/ .
 The Traction 
 Revenue grew 5x over the past year, and Lily has driven over $200M in new annual sales for a single customer. We serve some of the largest operators in our industries, including SRS Distribution (part of The Home Depot family), United Rentals, and Henry Schein, and we work closely with the Google DeepMind and NVIDIA ecosystems.
 How We Work 
 We work in small teams with real ownership: clear problems, direct access to the customers whose work you're changing, and room to ship. Your code runs in live production systems inside billion-dollar operations, so you see your impact directly. People who do well here want that proximity to the work. We're growing fast, and the people who join now shape what this company becomes. Everything runs on three principles: Customers, Culture, and Code.
 About the Role 
 We're hiring a Revenue Operations Lead to build the operating system behind our go-to-market engine.
 Our sales team is scaling fast, and everything underneath it has to scale with it: our data model, the forecast, the process reps touch every day. You'll own all of it. You'll turn our revenue strategy into territory and quota models the team can execute against, a forecast leadership trusts, and systems that still hold at four times the headcount.
 We build AI agents for a living and we expect our own operations to run the same way. Prior experience building with AI isn't required. Curiosity is.
 What you'll do 
- Own our revenue source of truth end to end, plus the integrations across our GTM stack
- Build the territory, quota, and capacity models the sales team runs on
- Produce the forecasting and reporting our leadership team, board, and investors rely on, and grade your own accuracy over time
- Design lead routing, qualification gates, pipeline hygiene, and the deal desk
- Own data integrity and attribution, so channel and investment decisions rest on something real
- Run commissions alongside Finance
- Be the first call for reps on process, data, and deal questions, and build the answers that keep that load flat as the team grows
 What we're looking for 
- 4 to 8 years in RevOps, Sales Operations, or GTM Operations at a high-growth B2B company
- Hands-on HubSpot or Salesforce administration experience
- Enterprise sales motion experience: long cycles, multi-stakeholder deals, low volume relative to deal size
- You build for what breaks at 4x, not what works today
- An instinct for what to automate and how far to trust it. Comfortable handing repetitive work to agents, and clear on what still needs a human

Our Mission
 Healthie is an AI-Native, ONC Certified EHR for modern outpatient healthcare. 
 Healthie is proud to power clinically excellent healthcare for over 40,000 providers who deliver clinically excellent healthcare - longitudinal and collaboratively, with patient and provider experiences at the center. Both healthcare and technology are undergoing unparalleled industry innovation, and it’s incredible to see the momentum - from consumers, from providers, and from reimbursement for this type of healthcare - grow exponentially. 
 We provide the powerful infrastructure every care delivery organization needs. On the surface this includes EHR, Scheduling, Engagement, Billing, Data, and much more. Underneath the iceberg are thousands of configurations, settings, widgets, automations, and limitless capabilities because we are an API-first platform. Our fully brandable platform makes it easy for clinics and organizations of any size to scale and never reach a limit. 
 Today, over 3 billion API calls are made to Healthie every month, as thousands of organizations who work with more than 21 million patients in total, rely on Healthie to deliver clinically excellent healthcare in over 35 specialties, from behavioral healthcare to complex chronic care management and personalized medicine.
 We believe in the power of technology to improve access to healthcare and we’re building the rails that make this a reality. We work fast and with quality because we provide business-critical, healthcare-critical software that clinicians and patients need for a better healthcare system. We’re customer-obsessed, operate with lightning-fast processes and responses, and always share our product roadmap publicly-  so customers can see what we’re building, and remain relentlessly focused on how care gets delivered.
 Healthie is backed by leading investors, and while we've $42M raised to date, more importantly, we operate with fiscal responsibility and have been profitable for more than half of our time as a company. We know that building an ONC-Certified EHR is a lifetime’s body of work, and we are here to build for our customers forever.
 Learn more at https://www.gethealthie.com/ 
 About the role 
 Revenue Operations is a core strategic function at Healthie, and our Customer teams — Customer Success and Customer Support — are where much of our next-stage growth is won or lost. As we scale toward $100MM+ in ARR, the customer lifecycle (onboarding, health, renewals, expansion) is moving natively into Salesforce as we migrate off our standalone CS platform. We need someone who can own that lifecycle end to end: design it, build it, report on it, and make the Customer teams faster because of it.
 We're hiring a  Customer Success Operations Lead  to own how our Customer teams run. You'll design the lifecycle motion with CS and Support leadership, then build it yourself in Salesforce — objects, Flows, automation, dashboards, and the integrations that turn Stripe billing, product usage, and support activity into signal a CSM can act on. This is a senior IC role with real ownership, not a ticket queue.
 The mix matters. You're a CS Ops operator first: you know what onboarding SLAs, health scoring, renewal forecasting, and churn-risk playbooks actually look like when they work. But you're also hands-on in Salesforce, comfortable building most of what you design rather than waiting on a developer. Where the build genuinely needs Apex, you'll scope it and partner with our GTM Systems Admin.
 You'll report to Bill Coffin, Director of Revenue Operations, and partner closely with our VP of Customer Management (Caseley), our VP of Customer Support (Justin), our GTM Systems Admin (Aaron), and teams across Finance, Product, and Engineering.

- Deep understanding of CS Ops workflows: onboarding, health scoring, renewals, ex

About the Company 
 Dirac is building the creative suite for manufacturing engineering. Manufacturing engineering has been underserved by fractured tooling. The work of defining how a product gets built is spread across process plans, MBOMs, routings, work instructions, spreadsheets, PLM configurations, ERP tables, and internal tools. Each artifact represents only part of the process, forcing engineers to rebuild context whenever a design changes.
 BuildOS brings these workflows together in one environment. Manufacturing engineers author, version, review, and distribute the Build—the canonical definition of how a product is produced.
 About Dirac 
 American manufacturing is burdened by inefficiency, bureaucracy, and outdated processes. At Dirac, we’re building a model-based manufacturing platform that connects engineering and production, enabling real-time feedback between design and manufacturing. By automating workflows and capturing critical operational knowledge, we help modern manufacturers move faster, build better, and scale complex systems. We are a mission-driven company of world-class engineers and operators with a culture of high agency, and high autonomy and radical ownership.

- Identify expansion opportunities across programs, teams, and business units
- Partner with product and engineering teams to support enterprise deployments and customer success
 Qualifications

- 2+ years selling enterprise software platforms to Aerospace & Defense manufacturers

- Proven track record of managing and exceeding $1.5M – $2M+ annual quotas
- Strong ability to navigate large enterprise sales cycles and multi-threaded deals
- Experience selling into legacy Aerospace and Defense primes and neo-primes
- Familiarity with core engineering and manufacturing software ecosystems including
- CAD, PLM, and ERP systems and related product development workflows
 Compensation 
- Base Salary: $120,000 - $150,000 + Equity
- On-Target Earnings (OTE): $300,000

 Location 
 This role is full-time and onsite in our New York City office (Empire State Building).

 Employment is restricted to U.S. Persons as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.15).

About Comfrt 
Comfrt LLC is the #1 Hoodie Brand in the U.S. and the #1 Apparel Brand on TikTok globally—built on a mission to support mental health and create everything comfortable for an easy, stress-free, cozy lifestyle. Our elevated basics are worn by millions and loved for their perfect mix of comfort, style, and cultural relevance. 
 About the Role:
 The Associate Merchant will support the Senior Merchant in driving the commercial performance of assigned categories across Comfrt’s growing omni-channel business. This role sits at the intersection of Product, Merchandising, Planning, Finance, Marketing, eCommerce, Retail, International, and Operations, helping translate product strategy into commercially successful assortments. The Associate Merchant will be highly analytical and execution-oriented, with responsibility for supporting assortment planning, sales and inventory analysis, buy recommendations, channel allocations, SKU setup, PO readiness, and launch execution. This individual should be comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where priorities move quickly and decisions are grounded in both customer insight and business performance 
 What You'll Do: 
 Assortment & Line Planning 
● Partner with the Senior Merchant and Product team to build and maintain seasonal and monthly assortment plans by category, collection, color, size, and channel.
● Support the development of line plans that balance core business, newness, seasonal programs, and innovation.
● Maintain accurate assortment information across product line plans and merchandising tools.
● Ensure styles, colors, pricing, launch dates, channels, and intended product positioning are clearly documented.
● Identify assortment gaps, duplication, and opportunities based on sales trends and customer demand.
● Support assortment localization across eCommerce, Retail, International, Amazon, and other emerging channels.
 Buying & Inventory Management 
● Support initial buy recommendations using sales history, forecast, inventory position, launch expectations, and planned sell-through.
● Prepare unit recommendations by style, color, size, and channel for review with the Senior Merchant, Product, Planning, and Finance.
● Monitor inventory levels and recommend reorders, reductions, transfers, or exits based on performance.
● Track incoming inventory against launch dates and identify potential inventory risks early.
● Partner with Planning and Finance to understand open-to-buy, inventory investment, and financial implications of recommendations.
● Help ensure approved buys are translated accurately into SKU and PO requests.
 Business & Sales Analysis 
● Own recurring analysis of category performance including:
o Sales
o Units
o AUR
o Sell-through
o Inventory
o Weeks of supply
o Margin
o Productivity by style/color
o Channel performance
● Prepare weekly selling recaps and identify key wins, misses, risks, and opportunities.
● Analyze new product performance versus expectations and provide actionable recommendations.
● Monitor core styles and recommend chase opportunities based on demand.
● Support hindsight analysis to inform future assortment, pricing, color, and investment decisions.
● Become deeply knowledgeable about the assigned categories and proactively bring recommendations—not just data—to the team.
 Commercial Strategy & Channel Execution 
● Support the Senior Merchant in determining the right assortment and inventory strategy by channel.
● Help build assortments for U.S. eCommerce, International, Retail, and emerging channels based on customer and business needs.
● Track channel-specific buys and ensure allocations are reflected accurately in internal systems and POs.
● Partner with cross-functional teams to identify incremental unit needs when products expand into additional channels.
● Support pricing and promotional analysis while protecting margin and overall brand positioning.

About Daylight
 Daylight is building a decentralized electric utility. We're building technology that enables homes to generate, store, and share energy with their neighbors, turning passive consumers into active participants in a smarter, more sustainable grid.
 Our team brings together energy and crypto veterans who believe in a future where communities power themselves. Backed by a16z, Framework, and other industry-leading investors, we're building the infrastructure to make that vision a reality. Learn more at www.godaylight.com 
 The Role
 In this role at Daylight, you’ll play a critical role in executing our Virtual Power Plant (VPP) and demand response program participation across the country. You’ll develop strategies to drive revenue growth, optimize asset performance, and collaborate with the development team to build an internal platform that integrates revenue stacking, analytics, and operational efficiencies.
 We're an early-stage startup, so this role goes beyond traditional asset optimization. You’ll support functions related to energy trading, pricing strategies, and risk management while ensuring compliance with program requirements and internal risk metrics. You’ll also develop partnerships and build operational capabilities to enhance commercial performance.
 This role is ideal for someone passionate about energy markets and technology who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You’ll shape our analytics platform, integrate key data sources, and develop risk management frameworks—all while having opportunities to grow into a leadership position as we scale.

- Monitor market trends, regulatory developments, and competitive dynamics to identify business opportunities.

- Develop partnerships with optimization and scheduling platforms to enhance commercial operations.

- Maintain expertise in ISO/RTO market structures, energy trading strategies, and risk-adjusted returns for contracted and merchant revenue scenarios.
- Assess the asset pipeline by market, development timeline, and commercial readiness, developing a roadmap for revenue optimization.
 What we’re looking for

- Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a related field (advanced degree preferred).
- 2+ years of experience in energy market analytics, trading, commercial operations, or asset optimization.
- Expertise in power markets, risk management, and regulatory requirements (experience with CAISO, NYISO, PJM, and ERCOT is a plus).
- Understanding of state-level programs (e.g., CA DSGS, MA Connected Solutions, MA Clean Peak Standard, etc.).
- Self-motivated with strong leadership skills and the ability to manage cross-functional teams.
- A results-oriented individual with a proven ability to prioritize tasks, manage their workload effectively, and deliver high-quality work with minimal supervision.

 At Orion, we are builders. Orion Services Group is building a skilled trades company: a growing network of commercial services businesses across the United States, spanning HVAC, electrical, plumbing, building automation, and related trades. We want to be the gold standard for people in the Commercial Services trades. We are highly acquisitive, partnering with 15+ operating companies per year, and we are building a 100+ year business with an A+ team. Our culture is low ego, high performance, and deeply committed to our people, our Operating Companies, and our long-term vision.   
 Role Description   
 We are seeking a highly driven and organized critical thinker to join our investing team as a full-time analyst beginning in August 2027. The M&A Investing Analyst will have responsibilities that span the entire deal transaction process and are beyond the scope of traditional entry-level investing and finance positions, including: financial statement analysis, financial modeling and valuation, investment committee presentations, transaction structuring, Letter of Intent negotiation, accounting, operational and legal due diligence, third party advisor management (lawyers, CPAs, consultants), debt financing, and seller relationship management.   
 The role is a unique opportunity to gain extensive M&A deal experience and leadership skills in a fast-paced and entrepreneurial environment. The role begins with in-depth training – working directly with Orion’s senior leadership to develop skills as an investor. Investing Analysts are expected to interact directly with sellers from day 1 and rapidly develop to lead transaction processes. Our junior team is given real autonomy in a collaborative, team-first culture, and we hire analysts who want to grow into future deal leaders.

- Expected to graduate from a 4-year undergraduate program in Spring 2027 (or Winter 2026).   
- Strong interest in M&A, investing, business, and finance with an analytical mindset and quantitative experience.   
- Strong desire to partner with founders and management teams to build leading skilled trades businesses, not just invest in them.   
- Minimum GPA of 3.7.   
- Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future visa sponsorship.   
- Strong communication and organizational skills.   
- Proactive leader with the ability to multi-task and work under limited supervision.   
- Intellectual curiosity and ability to learn quickly.   
- Sound strategic and critical thinking skills.   
- Enthusiastic team player with a positive attitude and high integrity.   
 Location and Compensation   
- This is a full-time role based in New York City, in the office four days per week (Fridays remote), with a start date in August 2027.   
- Base salary of $115,000 with a competitive year-end bonus package.   
- Successful analysts will have a significant amount of upward mobility through a variety of career paths within Orion, including the opportunity to grow into senior investing roles.

 Evio is a highly unique pharmacy solutions company that was founded by and works closely with health plans to implement transformative (to cost, quality, access and experience) initiatives primarily focused on specialty and other high-cost medication solutions.

About Thatch
 For most people, health insurance is something that happens to them: a plan chosen by someone else, with little room to fit their life. Thatch is changing that. We help companies give every employee a real healthcare budget instead of a one-size-fits-all plan, so people can choose the coverage and care that works for them, and employers get predictable costs they can control.
 It’s a simple idea, but making it real means solving hard problems across healthcare, payments, and technology, and we’re just getting started. We look for people who like solving complex problems, use good judgment, and are comfortable working through ambiguity. People here care deeply about our customers, take real responsibility for what gets built, and are driven by doing work that matters.
 About the role
 Thatch Market is growing, and so is the partner ecosystem behind it. We’re looking for a Strategic Partnerships Manager to own the partners already powering the Market and help decide who we bring in next.
 You’ll manage and grow our existing partnerships, identify where the Market should expand, and source and close the partners that can get us there. You’ll build deep relationships with our partners and look for opportunities to expand what we can do together, both within the Market and across Thatch.
 This is a high-ownership role with the opportunity to shape what Thatch Market becomes as we scale.
 What you will do
- Own our partner ecosystem. Manage our portfolio of Market partners, from performance and ongoing relationships to renewals, growth opportunities, and offboarding.
- Figure out what’s next. Understand what our members need, identify gaps in the Market, and determine which partners and categories we should pursue.
- Bring great partners to Thatch. Source, pitch, negotiate, and close strategic healthcare and service partners.
- Build partnerships that make sense. Structure commercial models that work for Thatch and our partners, with a clear understanding of the economics and tradeoffs behind them.
- Make partnerships work in practice. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other teams to launch new partnerships, solve problems, and make them successful over time. 
 What we're looking for
- 4+ years of experience in strategic partnerships, business development, or a similar role, ideally in technology.
- A track record of personally sourcing, negotiating, and closing strategic partnerships.
- Experience building and owning strong partner relationships after launch and growing them over time.
- Strong commercial judgment and comfort navigating deal structure, economics, and tradeoffs.
- The ability to see beyond the immediate deal and identify broader opportunities for a partnership.
- Strong cross-functional skills and the ability to move work forward across multiple teams. 
 Experience that stands out
- Experience in healthcare, benefits, fintech, or another complex industry.
- Experience building partnerships that are closely connected to a product or customer experience.
- Experience working closely with Product and Engineering to turn partner needs into scalable solutions.
- Unshakable optimism in the face of adversity.
 How we work
- We give people ownership and trust them to make good decisions.
- We move quickly, learn from customers, and improve continuously.
- We solve hard problems together, regardless of team or title.
- We care more about building the right thing than following a perfect process.
 What to expect
 We aim to keep the process thoughtful, rigorous, and efficient. Most candidates complete it within three weeks. You can expect:
- An initial conversation with a recruiter.
- A conversation with the hiring manager to dig into your experience and the role.
- Conversations with teammates across business development, product, and engineering.

Do you want to empower organizations to build smarter compensation strategies while ensuring fair pay for all employees?
 Syndio is the leading pay governance and compensation intelligence platform. We help organizations make better pay decisions at every stage of the compensation lifecycle, from leveling and offers to promotions and merit. Our platform gives HR, compensation, and finance leaders the data and decision support they need to govern pay fairly, compliantly, and with confidence. We partner with many of the world’s most recognized and respected enterprises, helping them implement leading-edge compensation solutions with expert guidance and analyzing pay for over 10 million employees across the world.
 Join us in our mission to help companies make smarter pay decisions they can trust!
 About the role 
 As our Revenue Systems & Operations Manager, you will own both the systems that power our go-to-market motion and the recurring operations that keep it running, and you will be measured on making that work progressively less manual. You will administer our Salesforce environment and the connected GTM tech stack, run the operational cadence that Sales and Customer Success depend on, and continuously convert repetitive processes into automated and agentic workflows.
This is not a ticket-queue administrator role, and it is not a purely analytical one. It sits deliberately between systems and operations. You will run the monthly close by hand once or twice to learn how it works, then rebuild it so most of it runs itself. If that sounds like the fun part of the job rather than the hard part, you will like it here. 
 Why this job is exciting 
- You will be the hands-on owner of the systems layer. Salesforce architecture, the connected GTM tech stack, integrations, and data integrity run through you. You will partner with the Director, Revenue Operations on roadmap and design direction, and as the person closest to the systems, your recommendations will carry real weight in those decisions.
- You will build with AI and agentic tooling. We expect this role to evaluate, pilot, and deploy AI across the revenue stack, and to build agents that remove recurring manual work rather than absorbing it.
- You will work across the whole revenue motion. Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing all depend on the systems and data you own, so you will see the full customer lifecycle rather than one slice of it.
- Your work is visible to leadership immediately. Commissions, deal desk, forecasting inputs, and territory design all reach the executive team. You will see the impact of good systems design in the room, not three layers removed from it.
- You will scale a function that already works. Your work is to make the Revenue Operations engine scale for our next phase of growth, not to build it from scratch.
 What you’ll do 
- Administer Salesforce as our system of record, including objects, fields, flows, validation, permissions, and data architecture.
- Own the connected GTM tech stack and the integrations between systems, treating sync integrity and data hygiene as monitored workflows rather than periodic cleanup.
- Own commission calculation and reporting, partnering closely with Finance on accuracy and exception handling.
- Run deal desk operations and audits, including approval workflow integrity and pricing and discount compliance.
- Own the monthly and quarterly revenue operations close, including data validation and reporting handoffs.
- Maintain territory and quota books through rebalancing, coverage changes, and mid-year adjustments.
- Identify the highest-cost recurring manual processes and systematically automate them, including automated reconciliation and exception flagging.
- Evaluate, pilot, and roll out AI and automation tooling across the GTM stack, and document what you build so the team is never dependent on one person’s knowledge.
- Partner with Marketing on the systems and data seams between marketing

About Block Renovation 
 Block Renovation is rebuilding the $500B+ renovation industry. We’ve built a nationwide platform that connects homeowners with high-quality contractors and brings transparency, predictability, and scalability to home renovation. Our mission is simple but ambitious: empower millions of homeowners to create spaces they love while helping thousands of contractors build thriving businesses. We are a fast-growing, technology-enabled marketplace operating across the U.S., and we’re just getting started.
 The Role 
 We're looking for a Rev Ops Manager to build and own the reporting layer that tells us what's actually happening in the business, and then to lead the highest-priority work that comes out of it. To lead high priority projects that drive our business forward, including building and owning the reporting layer that drives insights and steers direction across teams, distilling insights into solutions, and moving quickly to launch projects leveraging AI. 
 This is a highly cross-functional role for someone who thrives in ambiguity and is excited to solve problems across the business. You’ll sit at the intersection of strategy, data, execution, and AI, with direct visibility into the company’s most important decisions. Reporting to the COO, you’ll work across teams to identify opportunities, shape priorities, and turn ideas into
 What You’ll Do 
 Drive Revenue & Business Impact 
- Identify and lead the highest-priority strategic initiatives that drive revenue, growth, and efficiency.
- Use data and business insights to identify opportunities, size their potential impact, and develop a plan to capture them.
- Partner cross-functionally to take initiatives from idea through execution, owning outcomes rather than simply making recommendations.
- Continuously look for opportunities to improve conversion, increase revenue, reduce costs, and make the business more efficient.
 Own Business Reporting & Analytics 
- Own leadership, Board, and investor reporting end-to-end, including the underlying queries, data integrity, metrics, and first draft of the narrative.
- Build the reporting and analytical infrastructure that a clear view of business performance; including recurring reporting to run with minimal manual intervention.
- Be the analytical partner to Sales: own pipeline reporting, conversion and cohort analysis, rep performance visibility, and forecast support so Sales leadership can focus on coaching and execution.
- Own contractor network analytics, including subscription performance, profile health, supply and market coverage, retention, and churn.
 Turn Data Into Action 
- Identify trends, opportunities, and problems before they become obvious to the rest of the organization.
- Turn qualitative and quantitative signals—including support tickets, sales calls, and contractor conversations—into recurring insights that inform Product and GTM decisions.
- Partner closely with Engineering to translate operational and data needs into technical solutions.
 Build Operational Leverage & Automation 
- Own vendor and cost visibility, including contract inventory, renewal tracking, and spend benchmarking.
- Build scalable processes, systems, and workflows in partnership with the teams that will ultimately operate them.
- Lead cross-functional execution across Engineering, Sales, CX, Finance, and other teams to turn analysis into shipped outcomes.
- Use AI-native tools, automation, and reusable workflows to eliminate repetitive work and create leverage for yourself and the broader organization.
- Apply judgment where automation falls short—we value accurate, honest answers over confident but incorrect ones
 What We’re Looking For 
- At least 5+ years of experience revenue operations, business operations, strategy, consulting, analytics, or marketplace operations,
- A scrappy, hands-on operator who is willing to roll up their sleeves and solve problems themselves.
- AI-native: automation

Job Summary 
 The Sr. Hedging Analyst supports the firm’s hedging program by executing, analyzing, and managing derivative transactions and related risk activities. The role oversees the derivative trade lifecycle and supports the controls, reporting, and processes used to manage market risk. All work is performed in accordance with approved hedging strategies, risk limits, policies, and procedures.
 The successful candidate is highly detail-oriented, organized, and accurate in a time sensitive environment. The role partners closely with internal teams and external counterparties, brokers, and service providers.
 The role improves hedging processes and reporting through automation and data quality enhancements. It also analyzes derivative valuations, market risk, sensitivities, profit and loss, hedge performance, and new product or bespoke-structure proposals.
 Duties & Responsibilities 
- Execute approved derivative hedging transactions within delegated authority and manage the trade lifecycle, including pre-trade checks, trade capture, confirmation, reconciliation, settlement coordination, and issue resolution.
- Serve as a primary contact for trade execution and support matters with internal teams, counterparties, brokers, and service providers.
- Monitor derivative positions, market data, and operational deadlines to support effective hedge execution, timely processing, and adherence to established controls.
- Prepare, validate, and distribute recurring hedging, risk, and management reports; identify issues, control gaps, and improvement opportunities.
- Analyze portfolio exposures, market sensitivities, profit and loss, hedge performance, broker quotes, trade economics, and valuation outputs to support execution, risk oversight, and reporting.
- Support analysis of bespoke indices, payoff structures, and new products, including derivative characteristics, hedging implications, operational readiness, and reporting needs.
- Use Python, SQL, Excel, and related tools to automate workflows, improve data quality, and enhance reporting and trade support.
- Lead or contribute to enhancements of hedging processes, trading and risk systems, and reporting, including requirements, testing, implementation, and procedure updates.
- Serve as a subject matter expert on hedging processes and trade workflows, maintain process documentation, and support ad hoc business, audit, regulatory, and risk management requests.
 Supervisory Responsibilities:  This role does not have formal people leadership responsibilities but may provide guidance, mentorship, or subject matter expertise to others.
 Knowledge, Skills & Abilities 
- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, particularly when managing trade details, reports, reconciliations, and time-sensitive deliverables.
- Ability to follow established processes and controls, recognize exceptions, and escalate issues promptly.

 Compass International Holdings is seeking a Lead, Inventory Product, Data & Ops to make sure our inventory products work as promised across all ten brands, and to rebuild how that work gets done with AI.
 You will report to the Director, Inventory Product, Data & Ops. This team owns the technical and operational backbone of listing distribution: when a listing moves from an agent to the MLS, our agent platform, our brand websites, and portals, we make sure it happens correctly, on time, and per the seller's instructions. The Director sets roadmap priorities and MLS strategy. You own the operating engine underneath it: testing and validating what ships, helping build the AI systems that run our daily processes, keeping our reporting accurate, and keeping every workstream documented, tracked, and organized.
 This is a hybrid seat. You understand the business well enough to know what matters to an agent and a seller, and the technology well enough to sit with Product and Engineering, read a spec, and see where it will break. You are AI-first by default. Not someone who only uses AI to move faster on their own work, but someone who builds, stress tests, and deploys AI systems.

 Inventory Product Testing & Validation

You’ll own the measurement of how we acquire users across our portfolio of mobile apps and web properties — from attribution and channel performance to cohort LTV and payback — and turn that into clear recommendations on where to spend the next dollar.

- Design, build, and maintain common datasets and data pipelines that strengthen self-service analytics and enable data-driven decision making across the organization

 Collateral Analysis & Asset Diligence

 The Role 
 We are looking for a Senior Fraud Analyst to join our Customer Success team and protect the Mode Mobile ecosystem from fraud and abuse. In a rewarded app, users earn real money and rewards, so every fraudulent account costs us directly: rewards paid to users who did not earn them, partner reversals, wasted acquisition spend, and a worse experience for the real users who earn with us. How well we stop fraud affects our margins, our relationships with advertising and offer partners, and the trust of our community, which makes this one of the highest-impact roles on the team.
 You will review our fraud data, investigate accounts to decide whether they are fraudulent, analyze Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) and partner network data to find invalid and fraudulent traffic, and track fraud trends across our rewarded apps, with a primary focus on the Mode Earn App and EarnWise. Fraud in this space changes fast: multi-accounting, device farms, emulators, VPN and proxy abuse, bots and AI-driven automation, shared payout accounts, and offer manipulation all show up in rewarded apps. You will stay ahead of them by turning what you learn into rules, safeguards, and recommendations that stop fraudulent users while keeping the experience smooth for legitimate ones.
 You will work closely with Customer Support, Product, Engineering, Growth, and our partners, and you will be the team's expert on fraud. You will set review standards, mentor teammates, and report to leadership on fraud losses, trends, and results. We are looking for someone who is comfortable owning decisions, working with incomplete data, and measuring the impact of their work.
 Our AI-Native Team 
 Our Customer Success team, which includes Fraud, is AI native. We use AI in our daily work to summarize account histories, analyze large data exports, find patterns across large sets of accounts and events, draft case notes and reports, and speed up routine reviews. This lets us cover more ground than manual review alone, so analysts can spend their time on the hardest cases and on building better defenses. Analysts make every final decision on whether an account is fraud and review AI-assisted findings before acting on them. As a senior member of the team, you will help define how to apply AI  to our fraud workflows and how we keep it accurate and safe.

 Are you a sourcing professional who can turn strategy into action? ABB's Analytical business line is looking for a Global Category Manager to own the EMS/PCBA category and shape its global direction. 
 This is a senior individual contributor role with real ownership. You will consolidate the global strategy and supply base together with our factories, working across local, regional, and global teams to build a resilient, cost-optimized supply chain. The category is at a critical moment, and we need someone who can step in, build the plan, and deliver it. 
 What you'll do: 
- Develop and implement the global strategy for the EMS/PCBA category for the Analytical Business Line, including supplier footprint, risk mitigation, and cost optimization 
- Lead sourcing strategies using the CIPS process, ensuring the supply base has the capability and capacity to meet current and future business requirements 
- Negotiate agreements with key suppliers, renew price lists, and manage terms and conditions 
- Manage procurement planning, budgets, savings forecasts, and cost-out programs to reach financial targets 
- Identify, investigate, and select suppliers with focus on quality, delivery, cost, and sustainability 
- Provide ongoing contract management and oversight with suppliers 
- Ensure all relevant parties understand and execute the strategy, and that category sourcing performance targets are achieved 
 What we're looking for: 
 To be successful in this role, you bring proven experience in strategic sourcing and category management, ideally within EMS/PCBA or electronics manufacturing. You have a track record of building global strategies and, just as importantly, executing them — turning plans into tangible results on the ground. You bring strong stakeholder management skills, able to align factories, local teams, and global leadership around a common direction, and you have solid negotiation and supplier relationship management experience. You bring a data-driven mindset to analysis and reporting, and you approach your work with a collaborative, humble spirit that fits our culture. If you're someone who can both craft the strategy and roll up your sleeves to deliver it, this role is for you. 
 Why ABB: 
- A global role with real impact in a critical category 
- The opportunity to shape the supply base and strategy from day one 
- A supportive, hands-on team that values execution over slides

Investment Management - Investment Operations 
 A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE 
 As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact - touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world. 
 We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture on respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!   
 If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today.  
 At PGIM, You Can!  
 What you will do 
 In this role, you'll support the day-to-day operations that help investment portfolios run smoothly and efficiently. Working across a variety of asset classes, including equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, and derivatives, you'll help ensure transactions, portfolio activity, and investment data are processed accurately and on time.
 You'll partner closely with brokers, custodians, fund accountants, and internal business teams to resolve issues, maintain data integrity, and support critical portfolio activities. This role offers broad exposure to investment operations, asset servicing, reconciliation, and process improvement, providing an opportunity to build expertise while contributing to the overall success of the investment platform.
 This position is based in our office in Newark, NJ and will follow a hybrid schedule. Our organization follows a hybrid work structure ( 3 days in office) where employees can work remotely and/ from the office, as needed, based on demands of specific tasks or personal work preferences. Working from the office is encouraged when working on tasks that require a high degree of collaboration.
 Why Join Investment Operations?  
 Investment Operations plays a critical role in supporting the investment process and ensuring the integrity of portfolio activity across the firm. Associates gain exposure to financial markets, portfolio management, trading, custodial relationships, fund accounting, derivatives, collateral, and operational risk management while developing skills in problem solving, data analysis, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration. 
 This role provides a strong foundation for a long-term career within investment operations, middle office, fund administration, risk management, investment management support, or related financial services functions.
 What you can expect 
 Settlements & Transaction Support 
- Support the settlement of investment transactions across multiple asset classes, including equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, and derivatives.
- Coordinate with brokers, custodians, fund accountants, counterparties, and internal business partners to facilitate accurate and timely transaction processing.
- Monitor and resolve settlement exceptions, unmatched transactions, failed trades, and operational issues impacting portfolio activity.
- Research and resolve inquiries related to trade, cash, FX, and other portfolio activity.
 Reconciliations & Exception Management 
- Perform cash, position, transaction, and other operational reconciliations between internal records and external service providers.
- Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks through research, analysis, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders.
- Monitor operational controls and escalate material exceptions, processing breaks, or operational risks as appropriate.
- Maintain the accuracy and integrity of portfolio, accounting, and operational records.
 Asset Servicing & Portfolio Support 
- Support the processing and review of dividends, interest payments

You will explain complex concepts and influence others to adopt data-supported points of view while working on complex problems that require an in-depth evaluation of security controls and business context.

- Automate recurring data preparation, quality checks, correlation, and reporting where practical and maintain clear process and query documentation.   
- Continuously improve analytical methods, data sources, metrics, and validation processes based on stakeholder feedback and evolving risk priorities.

workday:R-125158.description:
Job Classification:
Investment Management - Investments 
 A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A CURIOSITY-DRIVEN CULTURE 
 As the global asset management business of Prudential, we’re solving financial challenges for millions of people around the world. To do that we need top talent, which we attract by fostering a truly collaborative culture in which everyone is encouraged to keep asking . We seek clarity and insight at all stages, from delving into individual security characteristics to understanding our clients’ investment goals at the broadest level.
 If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!
 What you will do 
 PGIM’s Strategic Capital Group (SCG) is responsible for providing institutional clients with asset-liability management, portfolio strategy, and asset allocation solutions harnessing PGIM’s multi-asset expertise across public and private credit. SCG oversees liability-aware portfolio construction and strategic asset design on behalf of its clients, while also partnering with other teams including PGIM Credit and PGIM Real Estate to deliver best-in-class private origination, credit underwriting, investment research, and risk management capabilities across a full range of asset classes. SCG is the investment manager for Prismic, a reinsurance platform launched by Prudential together with other strategic investors.
 This position is within the Portfolio Analytics team of SCG and will assume key responsibilities in the growth of our state-of-the-art quant platform for dynamic portfolio optimization based on rigorous asset-liability simulation and economic scenario generation. You will focus, in particular, on modeling the dynamics of diverse asset classes as well as underlying economic risk factors, which will feed into real portfolio construction projects, both for live deals and in-force business, not just post-allocation diagnostics.
 You will be based in our Newark, NJ office and will follow a hybrid schedule (3 days in-office).
 What you can expect 
- Build stochastic models to enhance and extend our proprietary real-world economic scenario generator
- Contribute to macro-factor and asset-level models that set key parameters within the scenario generator
- Develop advanced techniques to analyze emerging asset classes with sparse historical data
- Develop methodology and tools for attributing changes in asset-liability metrics to underlying risk factors
- Investigate and apply the latest quantitative and AI-based methods to concrete investment-strategy problems
- Work with teams across PGIM to properly model investment strategies across a range of public, private, and structured asset classes for use within our asset-liability simulations
 What you will bring 
- Economics or Finance Ph.D., advanced degree from a quantitative finance program, or comparable academic experience within a quantitative discipline
- Solid programming background, including Python (pandas, numpy, scipy) and exposure to modern transformer technology and foundation models
- Reliable knowledge of core quant finance topics: probability theory, statistics, stochastic models, options theory, yield curve construction, fixed income analytics, CAPM, etc.—both at the technical level but also conceptually, in terms of basic financial intuitions accessible to non-quants
 What will set you apart 
- Familiarity with structured products, private credit, real estate debt, and private equity, as well as previous exposure to insurance liabilities and asset-liability management concepts
- Knowledge about the theoretical foundations of quant finance and about macroeconomic frameworks
- Creativity, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to break down quantitative ideas for non-quant audiences
 *PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply. 
 Not

 The Senior Analyst will provide day-to-day operational support for PGIM Credit’s Securities Lending business. This role serves as a key control point across the loan lifecycle, supporting loan execution, returns, restructures, recalls, settlements management, and related issue resolution.
 In this role, you will partner closely with Securities Lending traders, broker-dealers, custodian banks, technology partners, and internal Operations teams to ensure timely, accurate, and well-controlled processing across cash-collateralized lending activity, including Corporate Bonds and U.S. Treasury securities. The successful candidate will bring strong operations knowledge, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a proactive approach to risk reduction, escalation, and process improvement.
 This position is based in our office in Newark, NJ and will follow a hybrid schedule. Working from the office is encouraged when working on tasks that require a high degree of collaboration.

- Monitor and support the daily settlement of securities lending loans, returns, recalls, restructures, and sale-related activity, ensuring timely resolution of exceptions and breaks.
- Act as a primary operational point of contact for Securities Lending traders, broker-dealers, custodians, and internal Operations partners across the loan lifecycle.
- Manage operational issues through resolution, coordinating across impacted teams and communicating status, risks, and required actions clearly and timely.
- Identify, escalate, and mitigate risks related to settlement fails, buy-ins, loan recalls, corporate actions, restructures, overdrafts, and client or portfolio impact.
- Support cash-collateralized lending activity for fixed income products, including Corporate Bonds and U.S. Treasury securities, in accordance with established controls and procedures.
- Analyze activity, trends, breaks, and key operating metrics to support management reporting, risk monitoring, and continuous improvement.
- Partner with technology and operations teams to identify automation opportunities, reduce manual risk, improve scalability, and enhance the overall control environment.
- Maintain strong internal and external relationships to support service levels, timely escalation, and effective issue resolution across the Securities Lending platform.
- Stay informed on industry initiatives, market structure changes, settlement practices, and regulatory developments that may affect securities lending operations.

Job Classification:
Investment Management - Investments 
 What you will do 
 As an Associate on the North American Distribution team, you’ll serve as a key partner to senior sales professionals, supporting their efforts to develop new relationships, deepen existing ones, and raise capital across PGIM’s investment platform. The role offers high visibility internally, regular interaction with clients, consultants, and PGIM investment professionals, and meaningful opportunities for professional growth and development.
 What you can expect 
- Support senior sales professionals in covering their territories and client segments—fostering relationships, advancing opportunities, and managing day-to-day business activities
- Prepare for and attend prospect and client meetings, including coordinating logistics, assisting in the production of meeting books and pitchbooks, and drafting meeting notes and follow-ups
- Partner with sales and investment teams to proactively identify prospects and prepare analyses that position PGIM strategies effectively
- Respond to client, prospect, and consultant inquiries, including data requests, strategy materials, and search-related information
- Coordinate responses to RFPs, RFIs, and due diligence questionnaires (DDQs) alongside the RFP, product, marketing, and compliance teams
- Conduct research and competitive analysis on institutional investors, consultants, peer managers, asset allocation trends, and industry developments
- Maintain accurate CRM (Salesforce) data—logging call notes, updating opportunities, and contributing to pipeline tracking, business metrics, and reporting
- Leverage core sales and research tools, including Salesforce, eVestment, Seismic, With Intelligence, FinSearches, Preqin, and various other industry databases
- Coordinate across Portfolio Management, Product Specialists, Marketing, Consultant Relations, Client Management, Sales Enablement, Legal, and Compliance to deliver accurate, approved materials
- Contribute to broader team initiatives focused on business growth, process improvement, and strategic priorities
 What you will bring 
- 3-5  years of experience in asset management.
- Familiarity with institutional investor types, investment consultants, and the manager search process.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and the broader Microsoft Office Suite.
- Experience with Salesforce or other CRM platforms, and investment databases such as eVestment, Preqin, or With Intelligence.
- FINRA Series 7, FINRA Series 63, and NFA Series 3 (or willingness to obtain)
- Progress toward the CFA or CAIA designation
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, Data Analytics, Statistics, or related disciplines; all majors considered.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build relationships and present information clearly to clients, colleagues, and senior management.
- Proven ability to multitask, prioritize competing deadlines, and work well under pressure with strong follow-through.
 Note: Prudential is required by state specific laws to include the salary range for this role when hiring a resident in applicable locations. The salary range for this role is from $95,000 to $130,000. Specific pricing for the role may vary within the above range based on many factors including geographic location, candidate experience, and skills. Roles may also be eligible for additional compensation and/or benefits.

 PGIM’s Institutional Client Group North American Distribution team sits at the heart of how we connect the world’s largest institutional investors—public and corporate pension plans, Taft-Hartley plans, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, and the consultants who advise them—with PGIM’s investment capabilities across public and private markets.
